blocks.text: Begin here

What might everyday life look like if the changes arriving with artificial intelligence brought more freedom, stronger communities and more time to enjoy ourselves? This is an invitation to explore that possibility by making useful things together.

blocks.text: This plan introduces the Community-Hour, or C-hour, and a connected community adventure beginning on Minjerribah, North Stradbroke Island. It brings local people and visitors together through food, creativity, learning, care, science and practical projects. Their contributions help build shared knowledge, useful technology and the capacity to look after one another and Country.

blocks.text: 1 Why Australia should begin now

Artificial intelligence is opening new ways to learn, create, organise and work. This plan connects that growing capability with Mutual Futures: shared ownership, more possible lives and a productive community in which people can learn throughout life, try different work and make room for care, travel and rest. Jobs and Skills Australia identifies substantial potential for AI to assist people in their work, with results shaped by how organisations adopt it and develop their practices. [E1]

blocks.text: The everyday scale of contribution

The supplied paper Unpaid Work, C-Hours, Societal Costs describes an incomplete ledger: much of the work that sustains households, relationships and community life is missing from ordinary financial accounts. Its sections 1.1 to 1.4 examine the scale of unpaid work, its uneven distribution and the consequences of neglecting it. That is a central foundation for this plan, with the statistical context updated below. [P2]

Survey changes mean these figures are not fully comparable with the older 2020 to 2021 figures used in the supplied paper. [E4]

blocks.text: Everyone everywhere and every day

The ambition is for everyone, everywhere, to be able to earn C-hours every day of their lives through meaningful contribution. Much of that contribution is already happening: raising children, supporting family, maintaining a shared home, helping friends, passing on skills and sustaining community life. A rostered event is one doorway into this system; everyday life is its much larger setting.

blocks.text: The author’s latest clarification governs the tone as well as the mechanics. This is a malleable thought experiment seeking input from real people as it becomes practical through pilots. Earlier editions used declarative record schemas, universal workflows and phrases such as “people can” or “the system should” in ways that sounded like permissions handed down by a central authority. Remember the circumstances of the people being invited: stress, overwork, fear, frustration, scarce time and money, and experiences of mistreatment by systems. Do not ask them to accept a declaration of trustworthiness. Frame trust as something earned through useful help, lower burdens, honest limits and responsiveness to their experience.

blocks.text: The author’s latest clarification governs the tone as well as the mechanics. This is a malleable thought experiment seeking input from real people as it becomes practical through pilots. Earlier editions used declarative record schemas, universal workflows and phrases such as “people can” or “the system should” in ways that sounded like permissions handed down by a central authority. Treat those passages as superseded design sketches. Future writing should identify whose idea is being explored, invite alternatives and leave genuine room for participants to change it. Preserve the author’s explicit non-monetary framing and personal sovereignty without inventing powers to regulate other people. Remember the circumstances of the people being invited: stress, overwork, fear, frustration, scarce time and money, and experiences of mistreatment by systems. Do not ask them to accept a declaration of trustworthiness. Frame trust as something earned through useful help, lower burdens, honest limits and responsiveness to their experience.
